figures.name: a sitting cat, seen from the side, with pointed ears and a raised tail
figures.how: I drew it on the integer grid: the square turned on its point as the head with the two small triangles as ears, the two large triangles joined into one big right triangle as the body, the medium triangle as front paws. The tail first hung off at a single point, so I moved the parallelogram to stand on the sloping back.
figures.seen_before: yes: the tangram cat is a well-known traditional figure, and the square head with small-triangle ears is close to the classic one, though I did not copy a specific diagram

figures.name: a house with a pitched roof and a chimney
figures.how: I worked on a grid scaled by the square root of two so that the square sits upright: the two large triangles make the roof, and the medium triangle, parallelogram and two small triangles tile a 3-by-1 strip as the walls. The square, left over, became the chimney resting on the roof slope.
figures.seen_before: yes: house figures are common in tangram books; this arrangement I worked out myself

figures.name: a fish swimming to the left
figures.how: The two large triangles form a diamond body; the medium triangle and the two small triangles make the fan tail. I tried the parallelogram as an upright dorsal fin and the square under the tail, which looked wrong, then laid the parallelogram flat along the back toward the tail and put the square below the belly as a fin.
figures.seen_before: yes: tangram fish with a diamond body and triangle tail are a familiar traditional figure
